source_text: Et exiuimus et uidimus ante fores Optatum episcopum ad dexteram et Aspasium presbyterum doctorem ad sinistram, separatos et tristes. Qui miserunt se ad pedes nobis et dixerunt: Componite inter nos, quia existis et sic nos reliquistis. Et diximus illis: Non tu es papa noster, et tu presbyter, ut uos ad pedes nobis mittatis? Et moti sumus et conplexi illos sumus. Et coepit Perpetua Graece cum illis loqui; et segregauimus eos in uiridiarium sub arbore rosae. Et dum loquimur cum eis, dixerunt illis angeli: Sinite illos, refrigerent; et si quas habetis inter uos dissensiones, dimittite uobis inuicem. Et conturbauerunt eos, et dixerunt Optato: Corrige plebem tuam; quia sic ad te conueniunt quasi de Circo redeuntes et de factionibus certantes. Sic nobis uisum est quasi uellent claudere portas. Et coepimus illic multos fratres cognoscere, sed et martyras. Uniuersi odore inenarrabili alebamur, qui nos satiabat. Tunc gaudens experrectus sum.
thought_title: Pleading leaders reconciled in the rose garden
orientation: Saturus is still telling his own vision of what happened to the martyrs after they were lifted before the throne.
pass_a_gloss: And we went out and we saw before the doors Optatus the bishop on the right and Aspasius the presbyter teacher on the left, separated and sad. Who threw themselves at our feet and said: Settle between us, because you have gone out and in this way you have left us behind. And we said to them: Are you not our father and you a presbyter, that you throw yourselves at our feet? And we were moved and we embraced them. And Perpetua began to speak with them in Greek; and we took them apart into a green garden under a rose tree. And while we are speaking with them, the angels said to them: Allow them, let them have relief; and if you have any quarrels among you, forgive each other. And they disturbed them, and they said to Optatus: Correct your people; because in this way they come together to you as if returning from the Circus and quarreling about rival parties. In this way it seemed to us as if they wished to shut the doors. And we began there to recognize many brothers, but also martyrs. All of us were fed by a smell that cannot be told, which satisfied us. Then rejoicing I woke up.

pass_b_english: We went out and saw Optatus the bishop to the right of the doors and Aspasius the priest and teacher to the left, standing apart and sorrowful. They threw themselves at our feet and said, "Settle between us, for you have departed and left us behind like this." We answered them, "Are you not our father, and you a priest, that you should throw yourselves at our feet?" We were moved with pity and embraced them. Perpetua began speaking with them in Greek, and we drew them aside into a green garden under a rose tree.

While we were still talking with them, the angels said to them, "Let them alone; let them have relief. And if you have any quarrels among you, forgive one another." They rebuked them, and they said to Optatus, "Correct your people, for they gather around you as if returning from the Circus and quarreling about rival parties." Then it seemed to us as if they meant to shut the doors. There we began to recognize many brothers, and martyrs as well. We were all fed by a fragrance beyond words, and it satisfied us. Then I woke in joy.
